title: Package metadata, dependencies, and features
summary: Declare a Rust package with a pinned edition, versioned dependencies, and an optional feature.

scenario.briefing: The campus command-line tool resolves a different dependency set on every machine because every version is a wildcard. Pin the edition and dependency ranges and put the optional clap dependency behind a feature.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.

hints: The [package] table needs name, version, and edition.
Write serde as a table with version and features.
Add optional = true to clap and enable it with dep:clap in a feature.
Run cargo test --all-features to compile the optional path.

misconceptions.testDescription: Dependencies use concrete version requirements and declared features.
misconceptions.feedback: A wildcard accepts any published version, so a fresh resolve can pick an incompatible major release. State a real version requirement and let Cargo.lock pin it.

misconceptions.description: Enabling an optional dependency in the default feature when most users do not need it.
misconceptions.testDescription: clap sits behind an explicit feature and the tests run with all features.
misconceptions.feedback: Default features are built by everyone. Keep optional capabilities opt-in so the common build stays small and fast.

misconceptions.description: Thinking a lockfile makes a wildcard requirement reproducible across machines.
misconceptions.diagnostic: Selecting the statement that a wildcard keeps builds reproducible.
misconceptions.feedback: Cargo.lock pins one resolution, but a regenerated lockfile can move a wildcard to any published release. State a real requirement.

sections.title: Metadata fixes identity
sections.body: The [package] table gives the crate its name and version, and edition selects the Rust language edition used to compile it. Cargo records resolved versions in Cargo.lock for binaries, so wildcard requirements still resolve differently when the lockfile is regenerated.

sections.title: Features describe optional capability
sections.body: A dependency can be optional, and a feature enables it only when requested. Features are additive, so enabling one must not remove behavior another part of the build relies on.

steps.title: Declare a Cargo package
steps.prompt: Edit Cargo.toml. Set the 2021 edition, pin serde with the derive feature, pin serde_json and assert_cmd, and make clap optional behind a cli feature. Run the tests with cargo test --all-features.

files.content:
[package]
name = "campus-cli"
version = "0.1.0"

[dependencies]
serde = "*"
serde_json = "*"
clap = "*"

[dev-dependencies]
assert_cmd = "*"

steps.title: Cargo package semantics

statements.label: The edition field selects the Rust edition used to compile the crate.
A wildcard dependency version makes builds reproducible across machines.
Cargo.lock records the exact resolved versions for a binary crate.
Cargo features are additive and should not disable behavior another feature expects.
An optional dependency is only compiled when a feature enables it.
Dev-dependencies are compiled into the released binary.

steps.explanation: Cargo.toml declares identity, edition, dependencies, and features. Version requirements bound which releases Cargo may resolve, and Cargo.lock pins the result for binaries. Optional dependencies sit behind features so default builds stay small.
hints: Use the manifest rules from the lesson.
